extracted.intended_audience: Reuters reporters, desk editors, and newsroom staff
extracted.subtask_description: Internal Reuters newsroom guidelines for writing, formatting, sourcing, polling, filing and editing stories, Top News summaries and media schedules; aimed at reporters and desk staff producing wire copy and web summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top News summary headline asterisk
rubrics_metrics.description: The headline must be preceded and closed by a single asterisk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related markets links toolbar placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The related markets links toolbar must always appear at the top of a TOP NEWS summary beneath the main TOP NEWS summary headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vertical bars in links toolbar
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical bars | must be used to visually group the links within the toolbar.

rubrics_metrics.name: No introductory sentence in TOP NEWS summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Never write an introduction to the news headline in the TOP NEWS summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top News headline category grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Story headlines should be grouped by one to four categories, and the first must always have the label "Top Stories" while any others can change depending on the amount and type of news on offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of headlines in TOP NEWS
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for 12 story headlines within a single TOP NEWS summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case conventions for categories and headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Category labels must be written in upper case, story headlines must be written in upper and lower case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story headline marker
rubrics_metrics.description: Each story headline must be preceded with a > symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not wrap story headlines; truncate
rubrics_metrics.description: Never text wrap a story headline to a second line, always truncate using ellipses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of dynamic cross-reference links
rubrics_metrics.description: Dynamic cross reference links to real-time news and prices must be grouped under the labels UP-TO-THE-MINUTE HEADLINES and LIVE PRICES & DATA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some summaries (e.g., Sports TOP NEWS) may not include LIVE PRICES & DATA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on cross-reference link columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Never exceed more than 2 columns of 2 cross reference links within a cross reference links category (i.e., UP-TO-THE-MINUTE HEADLINES).

rubrics_metrics.name: Static Speedguide links
rubrics_metrics.description: The static links to Speedguides at the bottom of a TOP NEWS summary should never change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Lynx Editor Glance/Take-A-Look
rubrics_metrics.description: In Lynx Editor, use the existing glance application to cut and paste headlines and USNs into a Glance or Take-A-Look; a Merge Headlines function may be added later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For examples of TOP NEWS summaries, key in TOP on your Reuters 3000Xtra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poll tagging and exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Only stories on Reuters polls should have the POLL tag and the word in brackets after the slug; every poll story Reuters runs is an exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-linked poll coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Polls linked to a set event in the future (company results, economic data, election etc.) should carry a PRE topic code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earnings poll tag
rubrics_metrics.description: Polls on company earnings should take an EARNINGS POLL tag in the headline and in brackets after the slug.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a poll subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a subject for a poll; it may be short term (next week's data) or long term (year-end index level), and need not be purely numerical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: analysts' stock index forecasts, rating performance of central bank governors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write clear, unambiguous, fair poll questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set your questions so they are clear, unambiguous and fair; leading questions aimed at a pre-ordained answer have no place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select bona fide poll respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Find respondents who are bona fide, know what they're talking about and are willing to take part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polling decision makers or celebrities is harder and time-consuming than polling analysts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect poll responses reliably
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect responses by phone, e-mail or fax; analysts are usually easier to get responses from than decision makers or celebrities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse poll responses and present consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring the numbers to life: get people to justify forecasts or views and establish the consensus view where possible (mean, median or mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish highest and lowest forecasts and the number of forecasts; median usually preferable to mean because it is less distorted by outliers; Excel can calculate these.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't ignore minority views
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't ignore the mavericks; minority views this month can become conventional wisdom next month; watch for changes in expectations and explain why they changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish poll timing and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Say when your poll was conducted as timing can influence views; publish individual responses when possible because transparency is vital to credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster publication reduces the chance of being overtaken by events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Polling Unit for help
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need help in conducting or covering polls, contact the Polling Unit (phone/email provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scepticism about outside polls
rubrics_metrics.description: When covering other organisations' polls, beware of spin doctors, self-selecting (voodoo) polls, and commercially-motivated polls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about polls presented selectively by lobby groups or sponsored surveys that may serve as free plugs for sponsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and fairness primary principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy and fairness are the hallmarks of Thomson Reuters journalism and must never be sacrificed for speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check facts, figures, names, dates and spellings; provide enough context for balance and fairness; use disclosure paragraphs where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy includes coding and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy includes accurate coding, proper use of slugs, appropriate headline tags and consistent style, and getting the right facts backed by authoritative, unimpeachable sourcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the reader know how you know what you know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define target audiences and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters writes for professional (investors, traders etc.), media (broadcasters/newspapers/agencies) and the broader public; one version must serve all by explaining significance and context without being too basic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All readers want simple, clearly written stories that say what's happening and why it matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic story structure and weave context
rubrics_metrics.description: A good Reuters story gets straight to the point and has main elements (context, analysis, human interest, color) woven in from the top, not tacked on later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate lede type
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the lede style that fits the story: SUMMARY LEDE (5 Ws), WRAP LEDE (pull together updates), ANALYSIS LEDE (state an argument/forecast implication), FEATURE LEDE (anecdotal/scene-setter/question/quote).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick the lede that best delivers the essential news and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nut graph must explain significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Nut graphs answer 'so what?' — explain why the reader should care, give context, milestones, what is at risk politically/economically/financially and whether this is a trend or first-time event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the reader is new to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing: state what is known and how
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the reader WHAT you know, WHAT you DON'T KNOW and HOW you know it; source every new piece of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether information came from press statements, court documents, interviews, Reuters databases, or reporter/photographer witnesses; good sourcing protects file integrity and reduces legal risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use quotes to source, add color and move story
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes should source material or add color and should help move the story along rather than echoing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support your lead with a direct quote by the third or fourth paragraph where possible; avoid 'parrot' (echo) quotes and avoid 'broken' quotes unless words are unusual/contentious/colourful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid innuendo and guesswork in reported speech
rubrics_metrics.description: When using indirect speech, avoid words like hinted, implied, indicated, suggested or signalled because these interpret sources' meaning; don't guess at what a source means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grow the story logically in blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand items sequentially: write 2-3 subheads as building blocks; each block should add detail/data, a quote, and analysis or context and follow logically from the previous block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address what's changing, who the parties are and what's at risk; national/international is usually more important than local; forward-looking is more important than backward-looking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reread for accuracy and fairness before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reread the story to bullet-proof it: ensure agreement with headline, correct day/date, quotes and data exist for contentious ledes, clarity on how information was obtained, check all numbers and spellings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full company names, proper titles, RICs or ticker symbols are correct and web addresses work; check for balance and legal dangers and use a second pair of eyes where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a second pair of eyes and involve senior editors for problem stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask a colleague to read the story critically before sending to desk; problematic stories should be copyedited by a senior reporter, bureau chief or editor in charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing responsibilities and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: If you file a story to clients, make sure it hits the screen; don't 'file and flee' — remain available to handle desk queries and provide a contact phone number if you must leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If advancing a story, file a skedline and try to send sidebars/updates to the same filing desk as the original story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsbreak/Update/Feature story length guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: NEWSBREAKS/URGENTS: no more than 2-3 paragraphs (~100 words). UPDATE 1s: ~5 paragraphs or 200 words. Most Reuters stories: 300-800 words. Breaking updates/sidebars/intra-day market reports: no more than ~500 words. Final wrap-up: ~800 words. Features/Analysis: 800-1000 words. INSIGHT pieces: up to 1500 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desks will cut overwritten copy; short quick updates are preferred on breaking news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make headlines sharp and within length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines should be sharp and informative using an active verb and short words; avoid unfamiliar abbreviations and prefer conveying one idea crisply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline field turns red after 64 characters (limit includes headline tags such as UPDATE 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Slug composition and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Slugs consist of a packaging slug (same for all items in a package) and a wild/flying extension to describe a particular item; packaging slug should quickly describe the story in one or two words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good slugs catch the eye and should provide a strong pointer to headline and first paragraph (example: BC-PHILIPPINES-HOSTAGES/).

rubrics_metrics.name: 10 key words approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a list of 10 key words without which you could not write the story — these capture the essence and most should appear in the first sentence or two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place the crucial word early in the lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Count how many words before the first strong, essential word in your lead; if more than 3-4 words, rewrite so the crucial news word appears earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given contrasting two 42-word vs shorter leads to show impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: First sentence length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the first sentence has more than 25 words, be nervous; more than 30 very nervous; 40 is time to break the sentence; 50 is definitely too long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking the sentence is an easy way to shorten the lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support lead with a useful quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to support your lead with a direct quote by the third or fourth paragraph that strengthens the lead and pushes the story forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People rarely speak eloquently or succinctly — use one or two short quotes rather than several long ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tricks of the trade: block and chain writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't leave holes, group related information into blocks, write sequentially so each sentence connects like a chain, and use signposts to move to the next theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-heads to break up the story roughly every 200-250 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks for error-free copy (checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sending: confirm day/week/date; check all numbers and conversions; watch spellings and consistency; ensure a quote for contentious leads; full company names and RICs are present; check web addresses; make sure USN matches Alert; check for legal/balance issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If potentially libelous or legally dangerous, mark ATTN EDITOR to get senior review.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATTN EDITOR flag usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the warning flag ATTN EDITOR (or ATTN EDS) in the slug line or first line of text if the story may be legally dangerous or affect Reuters' reputation; explain reasons separately to the editing desk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desks should refer ATTN EDITOR items to the editor-in-charge; see Attention Editor items and Hoaxes for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities of the desk
rubrics_metrics.description: Deskers ensure stories comply with principles and procedures, prioritise stories, ensure proper sourcing, clear presentation, fairness and legal safety, and add value as mentors/coaches to reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deskers should 'read in' each day and may correct typos/grammar without reporter reference but must consult reporter for significant factual/interpretive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taster (slot desker) function
rubrics_metrics.description: A taster assesses incoming copy to prioritise urgent news, decides which stories can be filed quickly, which need attention, and which must be sent back to reporters; Alerts/Newsbreaks that can be filed quickly are checked and filed by the taster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-editing stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy editors typically work in stages: read for logical structure (relocate buried lead/context), assess accuracy and fairness (check facts and legal dangers), then check typos/grammar/math/RICs/URLs/dateline/USN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible the same copy editor should handle a full update series to minimise introducing errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filer responsibilities on the desk
rubrics_metrics.description: The filer checks coding to ensure stories reach all clients, has final say on coding, checks headline and slug before filing and ensures the story actually landed on target services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a desker rewrites a story, it's good practice to ask another desker to provide a second pair of eyes before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau support and cross-market coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Desks assist reporting teams and bureau chiefs in coordinating cross-market stories, may write breaking updates/wrapups/news summaries, and monitor external news sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deskers are encouraged to reinforce bureaux on big stories as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media schedule compilation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Skedlines must be in clear, unabbreviated English; include PIX/VIDEO/GRAPHIC notes in the SLUG; TIME must be in GMT (24-hour clock) and, for US schedules, add AP style local time; use templates from Global-Schedules-Templates to ensure homogeneity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule sections must use double-indents; 'See also:' sections must have a space after '+' and '-'. Corrections and changes must follow a specified parenthetical notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections notation for skedded stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections must be noted on any stories that are skedded and subsequently corrected using a parenthetical format showing identifier, movement, author and a note to editors about the correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formatting provided in handbook text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Report skedline notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Reports can be included on media schedules but not all subscribers receive them; note in the SPECIAL REPORT skedline that not all subscribers receive it and provide expected time and bylines/wordcounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example skedline format shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single vs multi-take filing and USN policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are to be filed in a single take in nearly all circumstances; a second take is only for additions like cross-reference information and must use the same Unique Story Number (USN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct injection and self-publishing restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters must not publish directly to clients without a 'second pair of eyes' and designated self-publishing arrangements must be agreed with the regional desk; regional desk retains responsibility and publishing rights can be removed for abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, anything beyond a Brief or Urgent must be filed by an editing desk; corrections to directly injected items should be handled by the regional desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-filing checklist for reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sending to a desk, reporters should re-read the story (especially the lead), check RICs, typos and grammar; use a second pair of eyes in the bureau; and involve the bureau chief or editor for problem stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These simple checks help move stories through editing more quickly.
